title: We’re reaching peak camera with the Sony A7R VI
summary: Sony's new A7R VI flagship delivers 66.8 megapixels with a new sensor and Bionz XR2 processor that break the traditional trade-offs of high-resolution cameras. The camera can handle sports, action, and usable 8K video recording, marking a departure from older high-res models that were slower and noisier. This advancement makes professional-grade resolution significantly more accessible and versatile for diverse shooting scenarios.
content:
Maximum camera. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge	

It wasn't long ago that shooting with a super high-resolution camera meant making serious sacrifices for the sake of all those megapixels. Enter the A7R VI.
Sony's latest flagship high-res camera is a 66.8-megapixel spec monster. In addition to its modest bump in resolution from the last-gen A7R V, it uses a new sensor and processor that unlock nearly any kind of shooting - from sports and action to usable 8K video. It's a huge departure from years ago, when high-resolution cameras were slower, noisier, and more specialized as a result of all those megapixels.

title: So much solar: Digging into the list of every US power plant that went online this year
summary: Utility-scale solar installations led new U.S. power plant additions this year, with battery storage systems in second place, while fossil fuel capacity additions remained minimal. The data reflects an accelerating shift toward renewable energy as the primary driver of grid infrastructure expansion. This trend underscores the transformation underway in how America's electricity system is being developed.
content: Utility-scale solar leads by a mile, followed by batteries. Fossil fuels, not so much.

zh.title: 太阳能激增:深入了解今年上线的美国电力厂

title: When housing is unaffordable, this artist’s device makes pedaling harder
summary: Brooklyn artist Justin Blinder created "Ground Truth," an interactive device that makes cycling increasingly difficult based on neighborhood housing affordability data. The work uses physical exertion to visualize economic disparities across the city, connecting personal experience to urban inequality. By making housing burden tangible through bike resistance, Blinder transforms abstract data into an embodied commentary on gentrification and affordability.
content:
Justin Blinder had just been laid off when he first came up with the idea for Ground Truth. It was 2020, two weeks before covid lockdown went into effect, and the Brooklyn-based artist and technologist had no idea what the future would hold. He started working for the food delivery apps, and as he was riding his bike across the city, he began noticing the stark differences between neighborhoods.

zh.title: 当住房无法承受时，这位艺术家的装置让骑行变得更加困难
zh.summary: 布鲁克林艺术家贾斯汀·布林德创作了名为《地面真理》的交互式装置，该装置根据社区住房可负担性数据使骑行变得越来越困难。这件作品通过身体劳动来展现城市各地的经济差异，将个人体验与城市不平等相联系。通过自行车阻力使住房负担具体化，布林德将抽象数据转化为对城市绅士化和住房可负担性的有形评论。
